programme.title: Artists and Models
programme.desc: Napoleon has fallen, and David is in exile. His star pupil, Jean-Auguste Ingres, seems set to assume the role of first painter of France. Ingres's superb portraits and exotic paintings of the nude have made his reputation. But he seems to be a man out of his time, and his career is marked by bitter conflicts.

programme.title: Ten Pound Poms: The Real Story
programme.desc: In 1947, Australia's Assisted Passage Scheme began. For just £10, people could start a new life in a sun-drenched land of opportunity, and over the next 25 years, more than a million took up the offer. The scheme's pioneers tell their story.

programme.title: Wildlife on One
programme.desc: David Attenborough takes a look at the unique approaches of several different animal species to motherhood. From the elephant seal mother, who loses 40 percent of her body weight during the four short weeks she has to wean her pup, to the seahorse female, who leaves giving birth to the male. Plus, the spider who sacrifices everything for her children - she is their very first meal.

programme.title: Eden: Untamed Planet
programme.sub-title: Patagonia: The Ends of the Earth
programme.desc: At the far tip of South America lies a magical realm that seems frozen in time: Patagonia, known as `the end of the world'. Voyaging from the high Andes to coastal fjords, to survive here you have to be as extreme as the country itself, either specialising in one habitat or being tough enough to live in them all.

programme.title: Treasures of the Anglo Saxons
programme.desc: Dr Nina Ramirez reveals the codes and messages hidden in Anglo-Saxon art by examining artefacts like the Sutton Hoo Treasures, the Staffordshire Hoard and the Franks Casket.

programme.title: The Bridges That Built London, With Dan Cruickshank
programme.desc: Dan Cruickshank explores the mysteries and secrets of the bridges that have made London what it is. He uncovers stories of bronze-age relics emerging from the Vauxhall shore, of why London Bridge was falling down, of midnight corpses splashing beneath Waterloo Bridge, and above all, of the sublime ambition of London's bridgebuilders themselves.

programme.title: Jimmy McGovern Remembers... The Lakes
programme.desc: Writer Jimmy McGovern looks back on `The Lakes', his 1997 drama that showed viewers one of Britain's most-loved beauty spots in a whole new light, riddled with crime, drugs, sex and adultery.

programme.title: The Lakes
programme.desc: Twenty-one year old gambler and womaniser Danny Kavanagh flees Liverpool for a small Lake District community and enters into the dark souls and sexual quicksand of the people who live there.

programme.title: The Lakes
programme.desc: The village is shattered by grief and guilt as it becomes clear that none of the children survived the rowing accident. As the community grieves, the finger of blame is pointed at Danny for being an outsider.

programme.title: Easter Parade
programme.desc: Don Hewes, one half of a great dancing team, is dumped by his partner the day before the Easter parade. Wounded, Don finds himself a new partner, chorus girl Hannah Brown, who he decides to make into a star in time for the following parade. Don switches his affection easily from Nadine to Hannah, but keeps his distance so he won't be hurt again. Hannah loves Don too, but thinks he's still in love with Nadine.

programme.title: Fiddler on the Roof
programme.desc: Oscar-winning adaptation of the Broadway musical about life among the Jewish community of a pre-revolutionary Russian village. A poor milkman, determined to find good husbands for his five daughters, consults the traditional matchmaker - and also has a word with God.

programme.title: HARDtalk Extra

programme.title: The Rolling Stones: Live at the Fonda
programme.desc: On 20 May 2015, at the Fonda Theatre in Hollywood, the band performed the entire Sticky Fingers album live in concert for the first, and so far only time, in their career.

programme.title: My Life as a Rolling Stone
programme.desc: Mick Jagger has spent 60 years as frontman for The Rolling Stones. He talks exclusively about his life in the band, from his first performances in local teenage parties to his creation of a stage persona that has defined the rock `n' roll singer.

programme.title: My Life as a Rolling Stone
programme.desc: Keith Richards has lived a life of legend and in this documentary he talks exclusively about his 60-year career as the lead guitar player in The Rolling Stones. Richards's brilliance as a songwriter and performer, along with his defiant hedonism, have made him a cultural hero to millions and helped to shape the whole idea of what rock `n' roll means.
